callouts.html: Band ratio = I(400) / I(peak) on the lamp-corrected excitation spectrum (defined on the concentration-series slide). Concentrations under each bar, in chronological order. * Attempt 1 is only an estimate: we had no accurate BCA or NanoDrop readings yet and trusted a 40 µM stock that turned out to be mislabelled.
What justifies the use of band ratio as our fluorometry metric?

Inner filter effect: at high concentration the sample absorbs much of the excitation light before it reaches the detected volume (and re-absorbs emission), so signal stops scaling with concentration. The literature reports it from about 5 µM. Here the I(400)/I(peak) ratio stays roughly constant at 2–4 µM, then climbs from 8 µM up.

items.cap: Lamp-corrected excitation spectra, normalised to peak = 1 (mean of n = 3 per concentration)

points.text: Band ratio = I(400) / I(peak), read off each sample’s lamp-corrected excitation spectrum (S1 ÷ R1)
I(peak): the spectrum’s maximum, ≈ 485–489 nm, the anionic chromophore band
I(400): the intensity at 400 nm, the neutral chromophore band
With peak = 1, each curve’s height at 400 nm is its band ratio: 2–4 µM lowest (≈ 0.10), 32 µM highest (0.146)
Dividing by I(peak) cancels concentration and lamp drift, but only at low absorbance: from 8 µM the inner filter effect lifts the ratio
Try it: click legend entries to hide traces, drag across the plot to zoom, double-click to reset

callouts.html: Band ratio = I(400) / I(peak). All three constructs (ssDNA, dsDNA, nicked dsDNA chimeras) at 10 µM in both attempts.

points.text: Asp133 sits in the rare left-handed α basin: WT +57, +16
Unclicked 2× Tet2-Et pushes it to +74, +2, about 17.5° out of the basin
After the click it returns to +60, +18, back beside WT

slides.title: sfGFP: backbone rigidity (RMSF)
slides.q: Does the spring deform the scaffold? Does the fold stay intact?

items.cap: Cα RMSF, aligned on the barrel core
Axial force clamp between the two Cβ atoms

explain.text: <dfn>RMSF</dfn> (root-mean-square fluctuation): how far each residue’s Cα atom wanders from its own average position over the trajectory, after every frame is aligned on the rigid core. Low = rigid, high = mobile. x-axis: residue number (2B3P numbering); y-axis: Cα RMSF (Å). Dashed lines mark the chromophore (CRO 66) and the attachment sites Asp133, His148, Asn149. One colour per system: WT, 2× Tet2-Et and the 27 / 40 / 40-nicked bp springs (n = replicates).

Axial force clamp: a constant force applied directly between the two Cβ atoms, a controlled stand-in for a spring. x-axis: applied force (pN); y-axis: Cβ–Cβ distance Asp133–Asn149 (Å). Blue: clamp on the unclicked protein; green: clamp on the clicked tether; orange: the DNA-spring chimeras at their modelled force. Compliance is the slope (Å per pN); the stiffness κ is its inverse.

points.text: The β-barrel stays uniformly rigid (≈ 0.4 Å on the strands) in every system
RMSF traces overlie each other; only loops and tethers move
Clamp: 0–20 pN moves the sites by hundredths of an Å; κ > 107 kBT nm⁻²
On the clicked topology κ ≈ 350 kBT nm⁻², so a 4 pN spring moves the sites only 0.03 Å
Answer: the scaffold is not deformed; structural integrity persists

slides.title: sfGFP: forces applied, force field vs model
slides.q: How much force reaches the protein, and do the models agree with the force field?

items.cap: Force measured on the bare duplex, restraint windows
Site displacement against modelled force

explain.text: A bare duplex, no protein, held at a series of end-to-end separations by a harmonic restraint between its two linker nitrogens. x-axis: the separation the duplex actually adopted (Å); y-axis: the force the duplex exerts on the restraint, ⟨k(r − x₀)⟩ (pN). Points are runs, lines are means. Dashed: the <dfn>Euler buckling load</dfn> π²B/L², the force at which a straight elastic rod buckles. Grey band: what <dfn>Zocchi’s kinked-rod model</dfn> predicts for the same duplexes.

x-axis: the force the spring model says each DNA delivers (pN). y-axis: the shift of the attachment sites against each construct’s own clicked control (Å); below zero = pulled together. Blue sfGFP, orange ubiquitin (preprint). Ringed points carry no spring at all (slack strand or arms that cannot close). A real force effect would climb towards the upper right.

points.text: Measured directly: 27 bp 28.0 pN, 40 bp 15.8 pN, 40 bp nicked 13.2 pN
That is ≈ the Euler buckling load (27 bp: 26.8 pN); up to 35 pN in the largest box
Zocchi’s kinked branch predicts only 2.4–6.6 pN: the force field gives ≈ 6× more
Every construct pulls its sites slightly together; displacement vs force r = +0.08, p = 0.81
The force-free ssDNA loop compresses the sites by 0.32 Å, as much as any duplex
Answer: tens of pN on paper, but the stiff barrel does not move; the model underestimates the force field ≈ 6×

slides.title: sfGFP: DNA dynamics
slides.q: Is the DNA kinked or coiled? Does it interact with the protein beyond pushing?

items.cap: Axis bend per base-pair step along each duplex
Base-pair opening against imposed curvature

explain.text: x-axis: base pair along the duplex in the chimera; y-axis: <dfn>axis bend</dfn> at that base-pair step (°), the angle between the local helix axes either side of it. Line: mean across replicates; band: ± sd. A <dfn>kink</dfn> is a sharp local break of the duplex, usually with a base pair opened: it would show as one narrow spike. Smooth bending spreads the angle evenly.

Bare 27 and 40 bp duplexes held at set curvatures. x-axis: curvature (° per base-pair step); y-axis: fraction of runs in which an interior base pair opens. Ticks are single runs (top = opened, bottom = stayed paired). Blue band: where our chimera sits; grey band: the type II kink range Curuksu et al. found by umbrella sampling.

points.text: The duplex bends smoothly at 4.8–5.2°/bp, nucleosome-like, with no local spike
Only 0.03–0.83 base pairs open at any instant: the duplex stays intact
Pairs start opening at 5.5°/bp and always open above 8.7°/bp
So the chimera is not bent enough to kink on this force field
The DNA touches the protein in 72–98 % of frames (50 nt ssDNA loop 93 %): local contact, not action at a distance
Answer: no kink, no coiling of the duplex; but the DNA lies against the protein

slides.title: sfGFP: why the force field disagrees with Zocchi’s model
slides.q: Does the force field contradict Zocchi’s spring, or only his kink?

items.cap: Zocchi’s two force branches (lines, τc = 34 pN nm, B = 200 pN nm²) and the force field’s bare-duplex measurements (points)

explain.text:
Zocchi’s DNA spring (Molecular Machines §2.15). A duplex of contour L = 0.33 nm × Nbp and bending modulus B = kBT·ℓp ≈ 200 pN nm² (persistence length ℓp ≈ 50 nm), held at end-to-end distance x, pushes its ends apart with:
 bent branch (x > xc): f = 10B/L² − kBT/(L − x) (eq. 2.203)
 kinked branch (x < xc): f = τc / [2R√(1 − (x/2R)²)], the slope of Ek = τc arccos(x/2R) (eq. 2.196), R = (L/2)(1 − γ²/90)
The rod switches at xc = L(1 − γ²/15), γ = Lτc/2B (eqs 2.188, 2.194), where its bending torque reaches the critical torque τc ≈ 27 (nicked) to 34 pN nm (continuous).

Why the model puts our springs on the kinked branch. ℓp ≈ 50 nm is far longer than the 6–7 nm the tethers allow, so the duplex must bend hard. For 27 bp, L = 8.9 nm and γ = 0.76, so xc = 86 Å; the chimeras span 63–73 Å, below xc, so Zocchi predicts a kinked rod pushing only 4–7 pN (27 bp, 6.3 pN at 70 Å; 40 bp, xc = 121 Å, 3.0 pN). In curvature terms: a rod kinks once its curvature reaches τc/B = 2.6–3.2° per bp, and the chimeras are bent 4.8–5.2° per bp.

points.text: The MD duplexes never kinked: 0.03–0.83 bp open at 4.8–5.2°/bp. Bare duplexes open a pair only from 5.5°/bp, always above 8.7°/bp, i.e. an effective τc ≈ 58–92 pN nm, 2–3× Zocchi’s
So the force field was compared with the Euler buckling load F = π²B/L² (eq. 2.169): a rod bent smoothly, never kinked (27 bp 24.9 pN, 40 bp 11.3 pN)
That is Zocchi’s bent branch. Once kBT/(L − x) is small, f → 10B/L², and 10 vs π² = 9.87 differ by 1.3 % (the book calls 10B/L² “within 2 % of π²B/L²”)
Measured: 27 bp 28.0 pN (bent branch 23–25), 40 bp 15.8 pN (10.6–11.3): on the bent branch within 1.0–1.4×, not the kinked 3–7 pN
Answer: same elasticity, same B, same force law. They differ only in the critical torque: OL15 on 50 ns holds the duplex unkinked well past Zocchi’s τc, so it never reaches his softened branch

items.cap: Backbone φ/ψ at the two modified sites

explain.text: <dfn>Ramachandran plot</dfn>: every dot is one simulation frame, placed by the two backbone dihedral angles of a single residue. <dfn>φ (phi)</dfn>, x-axis: rotation about the N–Cα bond. <dfn>ψ (psi)</dfn>, y-axis: rotation about the Cα–C bond. Both run −180° to +180°. The boxes are the allowed regions: β / PPII (extended strand), right-handed α (helix) and left-handed α (rare; mostly Gly, Asp, Asn). Large symbols are each system’s mean. If a modification strains the backbone, its cloud leaves the WT basin. The star is the AlphaFold starting model.

Left: Asp7 (construct D6X), on the flexible N-terminal tail. Right: Asn553 (N552X), in the first turn of HEAT 14’s helix. Colours: blue apo Aα, orange 2× Tet2-Et unclicked, dark green clicked no DNA, teal 50 nt ssDNA loop, amber 50 bp dsDNA loop.

points.text: Asp7 starts in left-handed α (+65, +57), on the floppy tail (pLDDT 52)
Unclicked 2× Tet2-Et flips it to right-handed α: −53, −46
Clicked (+35, +53) and the ssDNA loop (+49, +33) put it back in left-handed α
With the dsDNA loop it spreads widely: −60, +38, sd 78° / 73°
Asn553 stays helical (−52 to −60, −29 to −46) except with dsDNA (−69, +2, sd 40° / 79°)
Answer: once clicked the tet groups barely matter; only the dsDNA loop disturbs the sites

slides.title: PP2A: backbone rigidity (RMSF)
slides.q: Does the spring deform the scaffold? Does the fold stay intact?

items.cap: Cα RMSF aligned on the core, HEAT repeats shaded
Bend and twist per HEAT repeat; horseshoe aperture

explain.text: <dfn>RMSF</dfn> (root-mean-square fluctuation): how far each residue’s Cα atom wanders from its own average position over the trajectory, after every frame is aligned on the rigid core. Low = rigid, high = mobile. x-axis: residue (UniProt numbering), HEAT repeats 1–15 shaded and numbered along the top; y-axis: Cα RMSF (Å), aligned on the core (residues 14–589). Dashed lines: the attachment sites Asp7 and Asn553. Apo, unclicked, clicked and 50 nt ssDNA are drawn; the 50 bp dsDNA run is off this scale.

Left: <dfn>bend</dfn> at each HEAT repeat, the angle between the solenoid axis entering and leaving it (°). Middle: <dfn>superhelical twist</dfn> per step (°). Right: the horseshoe <dfn>aperture</dfn>, the HEAT1–HEAT15 centroid distance over time (Å); dotted line: 62.7 Å in the B56γ holoenzyme (Day et al.). Same colours; amber is the 50 bp dsDNA loop.

points.text: Core RMSF 2.1–2.6 Å for apo, tet, clicked and ssDNA; only the N-tail (residues 1–13) moves 10+ Å
HEAT 12 is the most variable repeat, the hinge region the literature reports (HEAT 11–13)
With ssDNA the aperture changes by only +0.8 ± 2.8 Å (p = 0.77)
The 50 bp dsDNA run comes apart: core RMSD 48 Å, helix fraction 0.26 (0.77 elsewhere), aperture 127 ± 43 Å
Along the spring coordinate κ ≈ 1–2 kBT nm⁻², about 100× softer than sfGFP’s barrel
Answer: a single strand leaves the horseshoe intact; in this one 500 ns run the dsDNA loop unfolds it

slides.title: PP2A: forces applied, force field vs model
slides.q: How much force reaches the protein, and do the models agree with the force field?

items.cap: Cβ7–Cβ553 against the clicked zero
Bare-strand restraint windows against the models

explain.text: <dfn>Cβ7–Cβ553</dfn>: the distance between the β-carbons of the two attachment residues, the coordinate the spring acts along (Å). Symbol: each system’s mean; thin line: its full range; bars: block SEM. <dfn>Δ</dfn> is the shift from the clicked protein without DNA (the right zero), with Welch’s p on ten block means.

x-axis: the spring’s end-to-end distance (Å); y-axis: force on the anchors (pN), + pushes them apart, − pulls them together. Lines are models: <dfn>Marko–Siggia</dfn> (worm-like chain: a single strand is an entropic spring that can only pull) and <dfn>Zocchi f(x)</dfn> (a bent duplex rod that pushes, and softens once it kinks). Points: forces measured on the bare strands held at 60 / 80 / 100 Å. Shading: where each chimera actually sits.

points.text: Against the clicked zero, ssDNA: −3.1 ± 3.5 Å (p = 0.39), not resolved
dsDNA: +34.4 ± 8.8 Å (p = 0.003): the sites are pushed apart, as the horseshoe unfolds
The strand sits at 95 Å, its own rms size: Marko–Siggia gives a 1.74 pN pull
Bare ss50 agrees with Marko–Siggia within error (−1.23 ± 1.70 pN at 100 Å)
Bare ds50 pushes +10 to +13 pN at 60–100 Å, about 13× Zocchi’s 0.9 pN
Answer: the duplex pushes far harder than modelled; a single strand pulls weakly and moves nothing measurable

slides.title: PP2A: DNA dynamics
slides.q: Is the DNA kinked or coiled? Does it interact with the protein beyond pulling?

items.cap: Bend, sharp turns, torsions and stacking along each strand
Strand size and modelled force over time

explain.text: Top row: 50 nt ssDNA; bottom row: the modified strand of the 50 bp dsDNA. Left: <dfn>bend</dfn> of the C4′ backbone trace at each nucleotide (°); pink bars (right axis): fraction of frames with a sharp > 90° turn, i.e. a <dfn>kink</dfn>. Middle: <dfn>BII fraction</dfn> (backbone torsion ε − ζ > 0, a sign of local strain) and how often a base is <dfn>unstacked</dfn> from its neighbour. Right: mean curvature against end-to-end distance; dotted lines: kink thresholds 2.6 (Zocchi), 5.5 (onset), 8.7 °/bp (certain).

Left: each strand’s end-to-end distance over time (Å, solid) and radius of gyration (dotted). Grey line: the rms size of a free 50-mer (94 Å); a single strand at that size is neither slack nor taut. Right: the force the models assign frame by frame (pN): Marko–Siggia pull for ssDNA, Zocchi push for dsDNA (drawn negative).

points.text: ssDNA end-to-end 95 ± 9 Å, right at its free rms size: neither slack nor taut
Sharp turns in 18 % of frames, hottest at nt 3 by the tether: no interior kink
78 % of adjacent bases stay stacked; 15 % of the backbone in BII
3 of 50 nt touch the protein at any time, mostly the N-tail (Met1–Asp5, Tet sites, Gln557)
dsDNA: 8.4°/bp with ≈ 36 base pairs open on average: the duplex melts rather than kinking cleanly
Answer: the strand is a relaxed coil that touches the protein; the dsDNA loop comes apart
